tierNote: Tier 2 (ADR-0013): these objectives and the alert rules generated from them are parsed and asserted by apps/api/src/fitness/observability-rules.spec.ts. No alert has fired, nothing evaluates them, and nothing pages anyone (D132).

burnWindows.spends: 2% of the 28-day budget in an hour
5% of the budget in six hours
the whole budget at exactly the rate that exhausts it

objectives.name: Requests are answered without a server error
objectives.why: The beta's own figure, not the NFR's: 99.5% over 28 days is about 3.4 hours of 5xx, which two hundred students tolerate and which a single host with no standby can keep.

objectives.name: A read is answered within 200 ms
objectives.why: PER-08's target is a p95, so the objective is that 95% of reads are under it.

objectives.name: A write is answered within 300 ms
objectives.why: PER-09's p95. Sign-in is a write and a password hash; the load test found it close to this under a stampede (D129).

objectives.name: The concept map is read within 500 ms
objectives.why: PER-16's p95, on the route that serves it.

objectives.name: No message waits more than a minute for the relay
objectives.why: PER-13 asks for a result within 60 s of submission. The API does not time that end to end; the age of the oldest message the relay has not delivered is the part of it that can queue, and it is a gauge, so it is averaged over the window and not rated.

objectives.name: The synthetic probe signs in and reads
objectives.why: The probe (tools/stack-journey/probe.mjs) is the one check made from outside, through the proxy; the others are the API's account of itself. A host that cannot be reached answers none of them.
